newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland says U.S. funds bought most of yankee bond.
newsitem.headline: Poland says U.S. funds bought most of yankee bond.

text.p: Poland's $400 million yankee bond issue, placed on Thursday, was mainly bought by U.S. insurance firms, pension and investment funds, the finance ministry said on Friday.

"American insurance companies, pension and investment funds were the main buyers of the bonds... A small part of the issue, less than 10 percent, was bought by European and Asian investors," the ministry said in a statement.

On Thursday, Poland placed $300 million worth of seven-year bonds at 99.491 percent of the nominal price, with a 7.125 percent annual coupon, and $100 million worth of 20-year bonds at 99.299 percent of the nominal price, with a 7.75 percent annual coupon.

The issue, Poland's third international placement after two eurobonds in 1995 and 1996, was led JP Morgan Securities Inc. and co-managed by Merill Lynch and Solomon Brothers. It is rated BBB- by Standard & Poors.
The finance ministry earlier said its bond issue was meant to maintain Poland's presence on international capital markets and not because Poland needed cash.
Friday's statement said the ministry had at first wanted to issue only $300 worth of seven-year bonds.
"But considering signals of interest by investors in buying bonds of higher value and longer maturity, it was decided that the issue would be increased to $400 million," it said.
